# Upload performance and safer stack upgrades

This release improves upload buffering and PHP-FPM capacity, moves cache
traffic to direct connections, and adds local diagnostics. It also fixes
backup and upgrade behavior for existing installations.

## Upgrade instructions

Update the CLI **before** upgrading the stack:

```sh
kvsctl update-cli
kvsctl check
kvsctl upgrade
```

The first backup of an upgrade is made by the CLI already installed on the
server. Updating it first ensures that this backup includes your local
Compose override. This release requires `kvsctl 26.10.2`, including the new
cache migration and recovery support. Updating the CLI alone does not
install the new Nginx configuration or PHP-FPM image.

## Uploads and PHP-FPM

- **Keep standard upload chunks in memory.** Docker Nginx now uses a 10 MiB
  request-body buffer instead of the implicit 8 or 16 KiB default. The
  default 9 MiB KVS chunk and its multipart fields fit without an extra
  Nginx temporary-file write. Larger requests still spill to disk; the
  buffer is not the video size limit. This reduces temporary writes but
  does not establish the cause of every interrupted upload or HTTP 499.
  ([1454d98](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/1454d98))
- **Size PHP-FPM pools from memory capacity.** At startup, PHP uses the
  smaller of host RAM and visible container memory limits to calculate its
  worker and spare-process counts. Defaults budget 25% of that capacity
  at an estimated 64 MiB per worker; explicit settings remain available.
  Operators hosting several sites should divide the budget or set container
  limits. The calculated values are reported in the startup log.
  ([52e72a1](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/52e72a1))

## Cache connections

- **Connect PHP and cron directly to the cache backend.** New installations
  use `cache:11211`; upgrades migrate recognized loopback settings with a
  journal that supports rollback and recovery. Disabled caches and custom
  targets are preserved. Rerunning setup keeps an existing configured route,
  ambiguous configuration rewrites are rejected, and recovery can restore
  the journaled route while the backend is stopped.
  ([0a2f6af](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/0a2f6af),
  [938bb66](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/938bb66),
  [8b9c0ac](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/8b9c0ac),
  [7533aa9](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/7533aa9))

## Backups and upgrades

- **Include local Compose overrides in backups.** Manual backups and those
  taken by upgrades, rollbacks and replays now archive the operator's
  override alongside `.env`. Restoring the override is an explicit step;
  the CLI documentation includes the extraction command.
  ([a95447b](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/a95447b))
- **Honor MariaDB's shutdown grace period on the first upgrade.** When an
  older container still has Docker's short timeout, the CLI recreates it
  with the configured grace period before starting the other services,
  allowing MariaDB time to flush its data.
  ([6ca9b1d](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/6ca9b1d))
- **Account for backup free-space reserves before confirmation.** The
  upgrade plan now includes the backup's minimum free-space floor, reducing
  cases where a plan looked ready but its first backup refused to start.
  ([b579d03](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/b579d03))
- **Preserve custom bind mounts when rerunning setup.** An existing Compose
  override no longer triggers the old bind-mount initialization and its
  recursive ownership change.
  ([2fa3cbc](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/2fa3cbc))

## Diagnostics and networking

- **Diagnose the installed stack with `kvsctl doctor`.** Local checks cover
  configuration, container runtime, services and storage without changing
  the installation. Reports can be filtered or emitted as JSON; external
  network checks require an explicit option.
  ([060b790](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/060b790))
- **Persist Cloudflare visitor-IP configuration.** Docker single-site
  installations connecting directly from Cloudflare can use
  `CLOUDFLARE_ENABLED=true`; startup generates the trusted-proxy fragment
  from the persisted setting. Existing manual rules are preserved. This
  option does not configure HAProxy or Caddy multi-site deployments.
  ([9abff5b](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/9abff5b))

## Maintenance and release checks

- Refresh the pinned upstream images for Nginx, MariaDB and acme.sh while
  keeping the selected version tags. Dockerfiles and the release manifest
  use the refreshed digests.
  ([d9942c3](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/d9942c3))
- Check cache migration compatibility before publishing any image, so an
  incompatible CLI minimum fails early in the release process.
  ([4cbbb2a](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/4cbbb2a))
- Update Go dependencies and development checks; run CLI checks on every
  pull request and pre-commit checks on pushes and pull requests. Dependency
  updates now use Renovate with grouped updates gated by CI.
  ([4ec73b5](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/4ec73b5),
  [51323dd](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/51323dd),
  [4c350f9](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/4c350f9),
  [d63a1fd](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/d63a1fd),
  [f0deb1c](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/f0deb1c),
  [b0b4d10](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/b0b4d10),
  [e3ab8ac](https://github.com/MaximeMichaud/KVS-install/commit/e3ab8ac))
